REP WITH ME | Marketing Command Center

The Practice by InnerBoard | The Practice Club | Leah Roling

Let's make life sexy again. One rep at a time.

Every day the app drops a new rep. Every day I do it with you, on camera, out loud, and a little ridiculous. You are not doing your life alone.

1. Start here: how to use this every day

  • Open the 28-Day Calendar (section 6) and find today's date. It tells you the series, the rep, the hook, the script, how to film it, and the caption.
  • The app's rep always wins. Each day lists a backup rep written in the app's voice. If the app drops a different rep at 7 AM, use the app's rep with the same format and shot list.
  • Follow the Daily Routine (section 2). Morning story, film for 15 minutes, post, 30-minute engagement block, evening Close the Day.
  • Tick it off in the Google Sheet tracker (Rep With Me Daily Tracker) and log the day's numbers. Every Friday, update the rep counter.
  • North star: 10,000 reps done together by Dec 31 (tracked as public 'IN' comments + story tags + app completions).

3. The big idea: Rep With Me

Every day the Practice app gives everyone a new rep. Instead of just promoting the app, Leah does the rep with people, on camera, every single day, and invites them in. The content is the product working. The comments are the community forming. Nobody does their one life alone.

  • Campaign: REP WITH ME
  • Tagline: Let's make life sexy again. One rep at a time.
  • Community name: The Rep Crew
  • The ritual: read the rep, react, do it, invite. Everyone joins by commenting IN.
  • Closing line, every post: Life takes reps. See you tomorrow.
  • Hashtags: #RepWithMe #LifeTakesReps #ThePracticeClub #RepCrew
  • What 'make life sexy' means here: alive, confident, present, a little cheeky. Golden hour, the good perfume on a Tuesday, the pause that lets someone tell the truth. Life is the sexy part.

Fun rules

  • React honestly when you read the rep. 'Oh, this one's spicy' is better than a lesson.
  • Exaggerate the human moment: the most dramatic breath, the longest pause, the biggest no.
  • Let the app be a character. 'My app is bossing me around again.'
  • Always end with the invitation, never the lecture: 'Do it with me. Comment IN.'
  • Same closing line every day so it becomes a chant: 'Life takes reps. See you tomorrow.'

The growth engine: how we get to thousands of people doing reps

LeverHow
Comment-to-DM automationEvery anchor post ends with 'Comment IN'. Use a Meta-approved DM automation tool (ManyChat or Meta's built-in auto-replies) to DM the app link to every IN. Confirm the Practice app URL first.

Facebook Group: The Practice Club, Rep RoomDaily rep thread, Sunday Live, Friday wins thread. Moms of teens and practice owners are on Facebook.

Repurpose the showCut your Dr. Pat Show episodes into 30-45s clips with a hook line on screen. One per week as a bonus post.
Rep counterTrack IN comments + story tags + app completions. Show the running total every Friday. Road to 10,000 reps.

Look and feel

  • Palette: Warm ivory / cream, deep navy, antique gold accents, forest green for Practice moments. Never heavy pink.
  • Type: Fraunces-style serif headlines, clean sans body, gold italic for one emphasised phrase.
  • Feel: Premium collegiate club meets golden-hour lifestyle. Confident, warm, a little cheeky. Premium in experience, inclusive in spirit.
  • Merch: The Practice Club Tee (cream), The Club Hoodie (cream), Life Takes Reps Cap (navy), The Monogram Hoodie (navy).

Guardrails

  • Show the real app. Screen-record real reps and real coaching. Never fake an AI response and present it as real.
  • No unverified claims: no trial offers, pricing, outcomes or testimonials without approval and permission.
  • No em dashes in on-screen text or captions (brand rule from the Suite brief).
  • Sexy means alive, confident, present and fun. Never body-shaming, never thirst-trap. Life is the sexy part.
  • Grief, money and hard-season reps get warmth, not jokes. Read the room on the day.

7. Filming playbook

Kit: your phone, a small tripod, a clip-on wireless mic, a window. Optional: a dash mount and a second phone for Facebook Live. Edit in Instagram's Edits app or CapCut, captions on every video (most people watch on mute).

Setup A: Kitchen Counter

  • Phone on tripod at eye level, vertical 9:16, 4K 30fps, back camera (use a flip mirror or the Edits app preview).
  • Face a window, light at 45 degrees. Cream wall or open shelves behind you. Gold mug or flowers in frame.
  • Clip-on mic (DJI Mic or similar). Frame chest-up with headroom for captions.
  • Talk to one person in the lens. First line within the first second, no 'hey guys'.

Setup B: Car Confessional

  • Parked. Phone on dash or vent mount, facing a side window for soft light.
  • Best for raw, honest reps and 'I almost didn't do this one' energy. Engine off, AC off for sound.

Setup C: In the Wild

  • Handheld at arm's length, 1x lens (0.5x distorts faces), or hand the phone to a friend.
  • Grab 3 shots: you arriving (wide), you doing the rep (medium), your reaction after (close).
  • Wind muff on the mic outdoors. Ask permission before filming anyone's face; film hands, backs or reactions otherwise.

Setup D: App POV

  • Screen-record the real Practice app: notification, Today's Rep screen, the tap to complete (Control Center > Screen Recording).
  • Plus an over-the-shoulder shot of your thumb opening the notification with coffee in the other hand.
  • Always real app footage. Never simulate a coaching response.

Setup E: Golden Hour Lifestyle

  • The hour before sunset. Shoot 6-10 B-roll clips of 3-5 seconds each; 60fps for slow motion.
  • Wear the merch (Club Hoodie, Life Takes Reps cap). Movement in every clip: walking, laughing, pouring, spinning.
  • Edit to a trending audio in the Edits app or CapCut; one line of on-screen text, no talking needed.

Setup F: Two-Shot Duet

  • Two people on a couch or at the counter. Phone vertical, a step further back, both faces in frame.
  • Two mics if you have them. Film the 'before rep' take and the 'after rep' take for contrast.
  • Add the guest as a Collaborator when posting.

Setup G: Carousel Design

  • Canva template, 1080x1350 (4:5). Cream background, navy serif headline, one gold italic phrase per slide.
  • Slide 1 is the hook. Slide 6 asks for the send. Slide 7 is the end card. Max 25 words a slide.
  • Batch these on Sunday afternoons: they don't depend on the morning's rep.

Setup H: Live

  • Phone on tripod, light in front of you, quiet room. Go Live on Instagram; a second phone runs Facebook Group Live (or go live in the Group right after).
  • 20 minutes: 3 min welcome + wins, 7 min the week's theme, 7 min pick and do a rep together live, 3 min invite.
  • Save the replay. Cut the best 30s into Monday's story and the Facebook Group.

Every video: hook in the first second (spoken + on screen), captions burned in, end card with 'Today's rep' and 'Comment IN', closing line 'Life takes reps. See you tomorrow.'

Platform playbook (Instagram + Facebook, late 2026)

PrincipleWhat to do
Sends beat likesInstagram's head has repeatedly named watch time, sends per reach and likes per reach as the core Reels signals. Build every post so someone wants to DM it to a friend: 'Send this to your rep partner.'
Win the first 1.5 secondsHook as on-screen text AND spoken line in the first beat. A short reel watched twice beats a long one abandoned halfway. Aim for 15-40s on Rep With Me reels.
Carousels for saves and depth2026 benchmark reporting shows carousels roughly matching or slightly beating Reels on follower engagement, while Reels still lead on reach for accounts under 50K. Run both: Reels for reach, carousels for the crew.
Series beat one-offsRecurring, named series (Rep With Me, Rep in the Wild, Roll Call) train people to come back. Same opening line, same end card, every day.
Trial ReelsUse Instagram Trial Reels to test two hooks for the same rep with non-followers before sharing to your grid. Keep the winner's hook style.
Reply in the first hourReply to every comment in the first 60 minutes. Answer 'IN' comments with a heart and a one-line cheer. That is the community, not a chore.
Facebook is the 40+ living roomCrosspost every reel to Facebook Reels, but put the real energy into a Facebook Group (The Practice Club: Rep Room). Moms of teens and practice owners live there and comment in paragraphs.
Add Yours stickerEvery morning story uses an 'Add Yours' sticker with today's rep, so the rep travels from follower to follower.
